body:
INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW — codex-mockup-implementation-review

Candidate: 32f4c726424a6327393de26915d0e549ff308fe4
Parent: d295f4cd67a472d5a0cc295e1c163f5e97805e2b
Disposition: REQUEST CHANGES. This is advisory and separate from the formal candidate reviewer.

Verdict: 3 acceptance findings (2 implementation, 1 evidence/capacity gap) plus 1 type/API note. The exclusive direct/proxy/off-projection paths are substantially correct, the Intaglio boundary is upheld, and scope is exactly the stated nine paths. The candidate is not yet sufficient for the full cross-face contract.

WHAT I VERIFIED

- HEAD and parent are exact; git diff --check is clean; the checkout is source-clean.
- The diff contains exactly nine paths: README.md, app/index.html, app/smoke/smoke.cjs, AppCompiler.scala, AppView.scala, InteractionDecoration.scala, SvgDom.scala, AppCompilerSuite.scala, and SvgDomSuite.scala.
- Independent scoped run passed: sbt -Dsbt.supershell=false -Dstorymodel4s.grakern.build=/Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/grakern/.worktrees/pin-0329c43 app/test — 21/21 tests (SemanticZoom 6, AppCompiler 12, SvgDom 3).
- OnMark uses the compiler payload; Codex no longer uses ancestor fallback to decide direct styling.
- Proxy-only presentation has distinct classes/labels and does not set aria-pressed/current true.
- OffProjection returns no decorations.
- No story semantics enter Intaglio: no intaglio-module path changed, and InteractionDecoration itself is renderer-neutral.
- No new warning suppressor, unchecked match, cast, null, partial collection access, or exception was introduced in the changed main Scala.

F1 — MAJOR: a legal direct-plus-proxy target loses the proxy’s visible treatment

Evidence:
- SvgDomSuite.scala:67-87 explicitly establishes that one target may be Direct for a visible address and Proxy for another.
- app/index.html:31-32 declares line.selection-proxy first and line.selected second, both setting outline. The later selected rule wins.
- app/index.html:39-40 and 46-47 likewise give proxy and direct SVG rules equal specificity while both set stroke/dasharray; the later selected rule wins.

This state is reachable, not hypothetical. Selection is Set[Address]. At Story zoom, the existing battle situation is ViaAncestor; adding that visible ancestor itself to the multi-selection makes the same mark Proxy(original, ancestor) and Direct(ancestor). The DOM correctly retains both classes and the accessible label names both roles, but the computed visual style becomes only the direct dashed style. The promised non-colour proxy cue disappears. The same loss occurs on Codex lines/overlays once that face has a realizable shared target.

The unit test proves metadata, not visible distinguishability; no test checks the combined computed style. This violates the core ViaAncestor contract for multi-selection.

Required repair: encode the direct/proxy combination as an explicit composite presentation or use independent visual channels that cannot overwrite one another (for example, direct stroke plus a separate proxy outline/halo/pseudo-overlay). Add a browser assertion for an ancestor and descendant selected together on the same Atlas mark, and the equivalent Codex diagnostic case. The test must inspect computed style or a separately rendered proxy primitive, not merely class presence.

F2 — MAJOR: “fail closed” accepts phantom and partially missing renderer targets

Evidence:
- AppCompiler.scala:237-246 flattens all OnMark target lookups, then AppCompiler.scala:273-280 only asks whether the aggregate Vector[String] is nonempty.
- A two-mark OnMark where one mark resolves and one does not succeeds silently.
- A callback returning Vector("ghost-name") succeeds even if no such data-name exists in the lowered scene/SVG.
- SvgDom.scala:31-59 groups decorations, walks elements that actually exist, and never rejects leftover interaction names. A phantom target is silently discarded.
- The only negative test at AppCompilerSuite.scala:251-262 supplies Vector.empty; it cannot falsify nonempty-but-absent or partially missing targets.

Current WOG lowering likely supplies every name, and existing identity laws are valuable, but the candidate’s claimed fail-closed guarantee is not carried by this API or checked at the assembly boundary. A future lowering/name regression yields a green compile and no visible/accessible state.

Required repair: validate decorations against the actual lowered named-target index before yielding Compiled. Require each OnMark payload member—not merely the flattened union—to resolve to one or more appropriate targets, require every final target to occur exactly once in the relevant plate, and verify its navigation address equals Direct(original) or Proxy.visible. Add discriminating tests for (a) nonempty unknown name, (b) two direct marks with one missing, and (c) a proxy name absent from the rendered target set.

F3 — MAJOR ACCEPTANCE/EVIDENCE GAP: the browser court never exercises Codex ViaAncestor

The originating required court says the browser must confirm the ancestor is a proxy on both faces. The implemented scenario does not:

- smoke.cjs:521-531 asserts Atlas ViaAncestor and explicitly asserts Codex OnMark.
- smoke.cjs:602-607 again requires Codex OnMark in the horizon case.
- The new proxy class/ARIA assertions at 546-580 are Atlas-only.
- The pure “cross-face law” in AppCompilerSuite.scala:212-263 calls the generic helper twice with synthetic targets; it does not pass through CodexCompiler, pagination, PagedCodex lowering, SvgDom.inject, or Codex CSS.
- SvgDomSuite tests presentationFor only, not DOM injection or rendered styles.

I also enumerated the union of 698 app-reachable addresses from all 18 configured base artifacts (Reading/Overview × Story/Episode/Scene × Hidden/Sentences/Tokens). For every configured Codex flow, there were zero addresses where exactAnnotationsFor was empty while annotationsFor was nonempty. Thus this fixture/configuration cannot produce Codex ViaAncestor; the current green browser smoke has no capacity to prove that half of the contract. The same smoke does not exercise Codex OffProjection absence, although the pure AppCompiler test does cover both faces there.

Required repair: add a small admitted synthetic/diagnostic compiled flow or a focused DOM harness that produces a real Codex ViaAncestor through the full decoration, fragment, inject, and style path. Assert proxy class and non-colour style, original+visible accessible label, aria-pressed=false, aria-current=false, activation resolving to the visible ancestor, and direct restoration. Do not claim the full cross-face browser court until that path runs.

TYPE/API DISCIPLINE NOTE

The new InteractionRole and SemanticRepresentation ADTs are the right shape and preserve the meaningful decision. The guarantee weakens at Compiled: atlasInteractions and codexInteractions are both Vector[InteractionDecoration[String, Address]]. Raw String erases MarkId versus FragmentId, permits cross-face target swaps, and makes target membership a runtime convention. The new helper also reports stringly Either[String, ...], and public constructors permit Proxy(original == visible).

For this app-local slice, the minimum disciplined form is to retain MarkId and FragmentId (or distinct checked RenderedName domain tags) until SvgDom serializes data-name, and introduce a small InteractionError ADT for missing placement, missing member target, phantom target, duplicate target, and identity mismatch. If this abstraction is later lifted out, use smart construction to reject same-key Proxy and invalid names before publication.

PLAN RECONCILIATION

- Direct versus proxy ADT: upheld.
- Original versus visible address retained: upheld.
- Proxy-only ARIA truthfulness: upheld.
- OffProjection emits none: upheld in pure code.
- Renderer-neutral Intaglio boundary: upheld.
- Visibly distinct proxy for every legal state: silently fails for shared direct/proxy target (F1).
- Fail-closed missing target: only empty-lookup closed, not actual/per-member target closure (F2).
- Required both-face browser court: not met (F3).

SHOULD-HAVE-CHANGED

- The smoke or a browser diagnostic harness needed a real Codex ViaAncestor and Codex OffProjection case.
- CSS/composition needed an explicit Direct+Proxy intersection treatment because the new public presentation test declares that state legal.
- AppCompiler assembly needed the actual rendered target indexes; a nonempty Vector[String] is not proof that a render target exists.
- I swept every construction/match of InteractionDecoration, SemanticRepresentation, InteractionRole, and InteractionPresentation; no stale enum match or exhaustivity escape was found.

No file was edited, staged, or landed during this review.
